rationale: set_len on an uninitialized capacity buffer is replaced by a zero-initialized vec of the same length; no unsafe operation remains.
mem::uninitialized() for the hash table is replaced by a zeroed Vec; the uninitialized-memory hazard is gone entirely.
evidence_old: let mut htab: [usize; 1 << HLOG] = unsafe { mem::uninitialized() };

rationale: from_raw_parts_mut + read + set_len is replaced by resize/slice/read/truncate, all safe; the buffer is zero-initialized and then truncated to the written portion.
evidence_new: self.buf.resize(self.buf.capacity(), 0); let buf = &mut self.buf[b..]; let o = self.inner.read(buf)?; self.buf.truncate(b + o);

rationale: The one-past-the-end reference from get_unchecked is replaced by usize pointer arithmetic (as_ptr() as usize + len) with wrapping/checked overflow tests; no unsafe remains.
evidence_new: let data_ptr_end = data.as_ptr() as usize + data.len(); ... data_ptr_end.wrapping_add(cmp::max(IcedConstants::MAX_INSTRUCTION_LENGTH, Decoder::MAX_READ_SIZE)) < data.as_ptr() as usize

rationale: The unsafe wrapper around a call is removed, leaving a plain safe call, so the unsafe operation (calling an unsafe fn) no longer occurs at this site. The callee's signature change is not visible in the hunk, hence medium confidence.
The set_len(0)/capacity trick is replaced by storing Option-wrapped values and using len(); the vector layout is now consistent and no unsafe remains.
evidence_new: let values = Vec::from_iter(iter.into_iter().map(Some)); let space = values.len(); let ids = IdSet::new_filled(values.len());

rationale: The unsafe call to illegal_instruction is replaced by a safe call (function is now a normal helper), and a typed pointer plus saturating bounds check is added; the old unsafe operation is gone.
evidence_new: fn assert_user_ptr<T>(ptr: *const T) { if ptr as usize >= USER_END_ADDR { illegal_instruction(); } ... (ptr as usize).saturating_add(nbytes as usize) > USER_END_ADDR

rationale: The fix restructures insert_many around a size-hint guard and mem::forget(guard), but the new code still manipulates raw pointers (ptr.add, ptr::copy-style tail move) inside unsafe to move the tail; a safe replacement (e.g. slice copy_within / insert loops) is not what the patch uses, so unsafe code remains.
The raw-pointer write loop plus set_len is replaced by a single vec.resize(size, value); no unsafe remains and capacity and length are updated safely.
evidence_old: unsafe { let mut ptr = vec.as_mut_ptr().offset(len as isize); for i in 1..delta { ptr::write(ptr, value.clone()); ... } vec.set_len(len + delta); }

rationale: The raw make_accessible(base.as_mut_ptr().add(...)) call is replaced by the safe helper set_heap_limit, which performs the unsafe memory mapping internally behind a checked API.
The unsafe block around stack-state setup is removed; enter_wasm/catch_traps are now called safely with RAII drop of the previous runtime state, and no unsafe remains in the replacement.
evidence_new: let mut previous_runtime_state = EntryStoreContext::enter_wasm(store, &mut initial_stack_csi); ... let result = crate::runtime::vm::catch_traps(store, &mut previous_runtime_state, closure);

rationale: The forget + Vec::from_raw_parts round-trip is replaced by returning the owned Vec directly, eliminating the unsound length claim. Note the length padding to len is dropped rather than reproduced, so the job is done safely but with simplified semantics.
evidence_old: let p = result.as_mut_ptr(); unsafe { forget(result); ... let result = Vec::from_raw_parts(p, len, len); Ok(result) }

rationale: mem::uninitialized() is replaced by MaybeUninit::uninit(), the standard safe construction for possibly-uninitialized data.
PQcmdTuples/CStr::from_ptr/from_utf8_unchecked are replaced by the safe rows_affected helper plus checked to_str(); the FFI and UTF-8 unsafety is now confined to the helper.
evidence_old: let count_char_ptr = PQcmdTuples(self.internal_result.as_ptr()); let count_bytes = CStr::from_ptr(count_char_ptr).to_bytes(); let count_str = str::from_utf8_unchecked(count_bytes);
evidence_new: let rows = self.internal_result.rows_affected(); let count_str = rows.to_str().map_err(|e| Error::DeserializationError(Box::new(e)))?;

rationale: The unsafe PQgetvalue/slice::from_raw_parts construction is replaced by the safe get_bytes helper; the raw pointer work is encapsulated in a safe accessor.
evidence_old: unsafe { let value_ptr = PQgetvalue(...) as *const u8; ... Some(slice::from_raw_parts(value_ptr, num_bytes.try_into()...)) }

rationale: The unsafe PQfname/CStr::from_ptr block is replaced by the safe column_name helper; only a raw &str-to-pointer cast remains at the call site, and the FFI unsafety is encapsulated. The helper body itself is not shown, hence medium confidence.
evidence_old: let ptr = PQfname(self.internal_result.as_ptr(), idx as libc::c_int); ... Some(CStr::from_ptr(ptr).to_str().expect(...) as *const str)
evidence_new: self.internal_result.column_name(idx as libc::c_int).map(|name| name.to_str().expect(...) as *const str)

rationale: The free unsafe fn get_result_field(res, field) (with an unsound 'a lifetime) is replaced by safe PgErrorInformation methods delegating to self.result.get_result_field(...); the FFI unsafety is encapsulated behind a safe signature.
evidence_old: fn get_result_field<'a>(res: *mut PGresult, field: ResultField) -> Option<&'a str> { let ptr = unsafe { PQresultErrorField(res, field as libc::c_int) }; ... }
